name: MLflow
summary: An experiment and model lifecycle platform that records run metadata and artifacts, packages models through flavor-aware formats, and manages registered model versions.

features.name: Run metadata and artifact lineage
features.description: MLflow Tracking associates runs with parameters, metrics, tags, and files or models logged as artifacts; model registry entries can retain the producing run relationship.
benefits: Makes experiment comparisons and reproduction-oriented investigation queryable
Connects a model artifact to the run that produced it
costs: The tracking backend and artifact store become operational dependencies
Lineage is only as complete as the metadata and artifacts that callers log

features.name: Flavor-aware model packaging
features.description: An MLflow Model is a directory with an MLmodel metadata file whose flavors describe representations that different loaders or deployment tools can consume.
benefits: Separates a model artifact from the assumptions of one consuming library
Allows a single package to expose native and generic inference interfaces
costs: Consumers must provide compatible flavor loaders and environments
Multiple representations add packaging and dependency-management complexity

features.name: Registered model lifecycle
features.description: The Model Registry provides a centralized model store and APIs for versioning, aliases, tags, annotations, and lifecycle-oriented collaboration around model versions.
benefits: Provides a stable named boundary between producing runs and consumers
Supports controlled promotion and rollback-oriented workflows
costs: Registry metadata and permissions require governance outside model training code
A registry alias does not by itself validate model quality or deployment safety

mathematical_views.question: How can runs, artifacts, and registered model versions be related so that a consumer can trace a model back to its producing experiment?
assumptions: Run identifiers and artifact or model references are stable within the tracking backend
The model registry preserves the producing-run relationship
The graph abstracts storage transactions and access-control details

mathematical_views.model: Model-version state machine with interface projections
mathematical_views.question: How do registered model versions move through collaboration states while remaining loadable through one or more model flavors?
assumptions: A registered model version has a distinguishable lifecycle state or alias assignment
Each flavor projection has a loader contract and compatible runtime
State labels and aliases are treated as coordination metadata rather than proof of model correctness

costs: Tracking and artifact persistence add backend and retention costs

benefits: Interoperability across supported model libraries and serving tools
costs: Portable packages still depend on flavor-specific runtimes and dependencies

benefits: Named, versioned coordination point for model consumers
costs: Lifecycle metadata introduces governance and consistency obligations
